title: TEM: Temporal State Tracking Memory for Large Language Model Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.21900v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: An agent's memory must remain useful as information changes across conversations. A new fact may replace an earlier value without making that value irrelevant to a later question. We present Temporal State Tracking Memory (TEM), a training-free framework for tracking these changes. TEM stores facts as versioned records linked to their sources. It retrieves relevant versions, places them in source order and labels historical records before passing the evidence to the answer model. Event memory and original dialogue turns provide details missing from structured facts. We evaluated TEM on 420 questions drawn from 600 sessions involving 60 personas. Across four open-weight models, key-entity hit rates reached 75.71-97.62% overall and 96.67-100.00% on the historical-residence subset. Adding historical labels to otherwise identical, source-ordered facts increased overall hit rates by 17.14-55.95 percentage points. The evidence was compact: 94-

translated_title: TEM：面向大语言模型智能体的时序状态跟踪记忆
translated_abstract: 智能体的记忆必须随着跨对话中信息的变化而持续保持有用。一个新的事实可能会取代较早的值，但这并不意味着该值与后续问题不再相关。我们提出了时序状态跟踪记忆（TEM），这是一个用于跟踪这些变化的无需训练的框架。TEM 将事实存储为与其数据源相关联的版本化记录。它检索相关版本，按来源顺序排列，并在将证据传递给答案模型之前对历史记录进行标记。事件记忆和原始对话轮次则提供了结构化事实中缺失的细节。我们在来自60个人设的600个会话的420个问题上对TEM进行了评估。在四个开源权重模型上，关键实体命中率总体达到75.71-97.62%，在历史居住地子集上达到96.67-100.00%。在原本相同且按来源排序的事实上添加历史标签，使总体命中率提升了17.14-55.95个百分点。证据是紧凑的：94-（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: TEM提出了一种无需训练的时序状态跟踪记忆框架，通过将事实存储为带来源链接的版本化记录并标记历史信息，帮助大语言模型智能体在信息随对话演变时准确检索新旧事实，显著提升关键实体命中率。
en_tdlr: TEM is a training-free framework that tracks evolving agent memory by storing facts as versioned, source-ordered records with historical labels, significantly improving key-entity hit rates for large language model agents when information changes across conversations.
